## What a VLA is, in the words of the ones that named it

*(search)* RT-2 (Google DeepMind, July 2023) coined "vision-language-action":
a vision-language model "co-fine-tuned to output robot actions as natural
language tokens" — each of the seven end-effector degrees of freedom
discretised into 256 bins and written as integers, so that an action is a
string like "1 128 91 241 5 101 127" in the VLM's vocabulary. Two sizes,
PaLI-X 55B and PaLM-E 12B; the 55B generalised better. Open X-Embodiment
(October 2023) then pooled "1M+ real robot trajectories spanning 22 robot
embodiments" from 21 institutions and 60-plus datasets, 527 skills, and
trained RT-1-X and RT-2-X on it: the first evidence that data from other
robots helps yours. Its repository (read) licenses software Apache-2.0 and
everything else CC-BY 4.0; RT-1-X takes "a RGB image from the robot
workspace camera and a task string" and emits "seven variables for the
gripper movement (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, opening of the gripper)."

Everything since is a variation on one shape: a pretrained VLM backbone,
and something that turns its hidden states into a *chunk* of future actions
— discrete tokens (RT-2, OpenVLA, π0-FAST, WALL-OSS-FAST) or, increasingly,
a separate "action expert" trained by diffusion or flow matching (π0,
SmolVLA, GR00T, EO-1, EVO-1, MolmoAct2, X-VLA, WALL-OSS-FLOW).

## LeRobot — the framework the open ones live in

`huggingface/lerobot` README (read): LeRobot "aims to provide models,
datasets, and tools for real-world robotics in PyTorch." Policies listed:
imitation learning — ACT, Diffusion, VQ-BeT, Multitask DiT; RL — HIL-SERL,
TD-MPC; "VLA Models: Pi0, Pi0Fast, Pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, SmolVLA, XVLA, EO-1,
MolmoAct2, WALL-OSS, EVO1"; world models — VLA-JEPA, LingBot-VA, FastWAM;
reward models — SARM, TOPReward, Robometer. Robots: SO100, LeKiwi, Koch,
HopeJR, OMX, EarthRover, Reachy2, OpenARM, Unitree G1, reBot B601, plus
gamepads, keyboards and phones as teleoperators. Apache 2.0. The policies
folder on `main` (read) has 21 entries: act, common, diffusion, eo1, evo1,
fastwam, gaussian_actor, groot, lingbot_va, molmoact2, multi_task_dit,
pi0, pi05, pi0_fast, rtc, smolvla, tdmpc, vla_jepa, vqbet, wall_x, xvla.

**Hardware guide** (`hardware_guide.mdx`, read), peak VRAM at batch size 8:
light behaviour cloning (act, vqbet, tdmpc) 2–6 GB; diffusion 8–14 GB;
"Small VLA" (smolvla) 10–16 GB, "RTX 4080+, L4, A10G"; "Large VLA" (pi0,
pi05, xvla, wall_x) 24–40 GB, "A100 40GB+"; "Multimodal" (groot, eo1)
24–40 GB. Training times for five epochs over about 45k frames: act on an
RTX 4090 30–60 min; smolvla on an L4/A10G 3–6 h; pi0/pi05 on an A100 40GB
4–8 h; act on Apple silicon M1/M3 Max 6–14 h. On CPU-only training the
guide says: "Don't train. Use Colab or rent a GPU."

**Datasets** (`lerobot-dataset-v3.mdx`, read): a LeRobotDataset is
"Tabular data: low-dimensional, high-frequency signals (states, actions,
timestamps) stored in Apache Parquet", "Camera frames concatenated and
encoded into MP4" per camera, and "Metadata: JSON/Parquet records
describing schema (feature names, dtypes, shapes), frame rates,
normalization stats". A frame carries `observation.state`, `action`,
`observation.images.<camera>`, `timestamp` and a task string. v3 moved from
one file per episode to "Many episodes per Parquet/MP4 file", reconstructing
episodes "via metadata, not file boundaries."

**The robot** *(search: TechCrunch, Seeed, ThinkRobotics)*: the SO-101, the
3D-printed six-axis arm LeRobot's community trains on, was announced by
Hugging Face in April 2025 "starting at $100" for the motors and parts;
assembled kits and tariffs put retail between roughly $100 and $500.

## The models, one by one

Configuration defaults are from the LeRobot policy files on `main` (read);
they are what the framework assumes about each model.

**OpenVLA** (`openvla/openvla`, read): "an open-source vision-language-action
model"; 7B; "fused DINOv2 and SigLIP vision backbone" on a Llama-2 LLM;
"trained on a large mixture of datasets from Open X-Embodiment spanning
970K trajectories"; code MIT, weights under the Llama Community License;
inference in bf16 with Flash Attention 2; LoRA fine-tuning "approximately
27GB" of GPU memory; initial release 13 June 2024, updates to March 2025.
*(search)* The paper: outperforms the 55B RT-2-X "by 16.5% absolute success
rate across 29 evaluated tasks" (73.5% against 57.0% on the WidowX Bridge
suite). OpenVLA-OFT (February 2025): parallel decoding, action chunking, a
continuous action head and an L1 objective take LIBERO from 76.5% to 97.1%
and action generation 26× faster.

**π0, π0-FAST, π0.5** (`Physical-Intelligence/openpi`, read): "open-source
models and packages for robotics, published by the Physical Intelligence
team"; base checkpoints `pi0_base` ("a flow-based vision-language-action
model"), `pi0_fast_base` ("an autoregressive VLA, based on the FAST action
tokenizer") and `pi05_base` ("an upgraded version of π₀ with better
open-world generalization"), "pre-trained on 10k+ hours of robot data";
fine-tuned checkpoints for DROID, ALOHA and LIBERO. Hardware: inference
"> 8 GB" (RTX 4090), LoRA fine-tuning "> 22.5 GB", full fine-tuning
"> 70 GB" (A100 80GB / H100). `LICENSE`: Apache 2.0. Nothing after π0.5 is
in the repository. LeRobot's `pi05` config: `paligemma_variant =
"gemma_2b"`, `action_expert_variant = "gemma_300m"`, `chunk_size = 50`,
`n_action_steps = 50`, images 224 × 224, tokenizer
`google/paligemma-3b-pt-224`. *(search)* The π0 paper (31 October 2024): a
3B PaliGemma backbone (2.29B fine-tuned) and a 0.315B action expert trained
with flow matching, on data from seven robots and 68 tasks plus Open
X-Embodiment. π0.5 (April 2025) added co-training on heterogeneous data and
cleaning unseen homes. π*0.6 (late 2025) used RL to run an espresso machine
through 13-hour shifts; π0.7 (16 April 2026) is "a steerable model with
emergent capabilities" — compositional generalisation, prompted with
language, metadata and visual sub-goals from a light world model — and is
not open-weight.

**SmolVLA** (LeRobot, read): "Hugging Face's lightweight foundation model
for robotics. Designed for easy fine-tuning on LeRobot datasets";
checkpoint `lerobot/smolvla_base`, "our pretrained 450M model";
`vlm_model_name = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct"`,
`num_vlm_layers = 16` (only the first sixteen layers of the VLM are used),
`expert_width_multiplier = 0.75`, `chunk_size = 50`, `n_action_steps = 50`,
images padded to 512 × 512; the model class is `VLAFlowMatching`, with
real-time-chunking (`rtc`) options for asynchronous execution. Fine-tuning
"for 20k steps will roughly take ~4 hrs on a single A100 GPU". *(search)*
The paper (2 June 2025): SmolVLM2-500M plus a ~100M flow-matching action
expert; pretrained on 481 community datasets, about 23k episodes and 10.6M
frames, mostly SO-100; pretraining lifted real SO-100 success from 51.7% to
78.3%; asynchronous inference gives "30% faster response and 2× task
throughput".

**GR00T N1.7** (`NVIDIA/Isaac-GR00T`, read for the previous article; LeRobot
`groot` config, read): base `nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B`, vision-language backbone
`nvidia/Cosmos-Reason2-2B`, `chunk_size = 40`, `n_action_steps = 40`,
images 256 × 256 with a 230 × 230 crop; `max_state_dim = max_action_dim =
132`; N1.5 support removed and the old 50/224 defaults remapped with a
warning. Code Apache-2.0, weights NVIDIA Open Model License; 16 GB+ VRAM
to run, 40 GB+ to fine-tune.

**X-VLA** (`2toINF/X-VLA` and `xvla.mdx`, read): "Soft-Prompted Transformer
as a Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model"; "a
soft-prompted, flow-matching VLA framework that treats each hardware setup
as a 'task' and encodes it using a small set of learnable embeddings";
X-VLA-0.9B "trained on 290K episodes spanning seven robotic platforms",
adapting with "only 1% of parameters tuned (9M)"; Apache 2.0; arXiv
2510.10274, ICLR 2026. LeRobot config: a Florence-2 configuration with a
`facebook/bart-large` tokenizer, `hidden_size = 1024`, `depth = 24`,
`chunk_size = 32`, `len_soft_prompts = 32`. Checkpoints `lerobot/xvla-base`,
`-libero`, `-widowx`, `-folding`, `-agibot-world`, `-google-robot`.

**EO-1** (LeRobot `eo1` config, read): `vlm_base =
"Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct"`, `chunk_size = 16`, `n_action_steps = 16`,
images between 64 and 128 patches of 28 × 28. *(search, LeRobot 0.6 release
blog)* "a VLA pretrained upstream on interleaved vision-text-action data …
a Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone with a flow-matching action head." The upstream
repository was not found at the guessed address and was not read.

**EVO-1** (`policy_evo1_README.md` and `evo1` config, read): "a
Vision-Language-Action policy for robot control" with an "InternVL3
vision-language backbone" and a "flow-matching action head", from MINT-SJTU;
`vlm_model_name = "OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B-hf"`, `chunk_size = 50`, images
448 × 448, `action_head = "flowmatching"`. *(search)* 0.77B parameters,
"small enough to fine-tune and run in real time on modest GPUs."

**MolmoAct and MolmoAct2** (Ai2; both READMEs read): MolmoAct (12 August
2025) is "Ai2's open-sourced Action Reasoning Model that can reason in
space" — it emits depth tokens and a *visual trace*, integer image
coordinates you can draw before the arm moves; 7B; Apache 2.0, with
weights, code and three datasets released. MolmoAct2 (5 May 2026) "builds
on the Molmo2-ER embodied-reasoning vision-language backbone, adds robot
state and action modeling, and connects the VLM to a flow-matching
continuous action expert"; base checkpoints, fine-tuned policies and the
datasets are released under Apache 2.0; "integrated into LeRobot as a
policy implementation"; deployable out of the box on "SO-100, Bimanual YAMs,
and Franka DROID".

**WALL-OSS** (`X-Square-Robot/wall-x` and `policy_walloss_README.md`,
read): "an end-to-end embodied foundation model" — "based on Qwen2.5-VL
with flow matching/FAST action prediction", a mixture of experts "with
action-specific routing"; releases WALL-OSS-FLOW and WALL-OSS-FAST
(September 2025) and a 1.1.0 in June 2026; Apache 2.0; LeRobot config
`pretrained_name_or_path = "x-square-robot/wall-oss-flow"`, `chunk_size =
32`, `prediction_mode = "diffusion"`. Parameter count not stated where read.

**Helix and Helix-02** (Figure) *(search; figure.ai blocked)*: Helix
(February 2025) is "System 1, System 2" — a ~7B VLM reasoning "at 7 to 9
Hz" and an 80M visuomotor policy at 200 Hz, trained on "approximately 500
hours" of demonstrations, controlling a 35-degree-of-freedom upper body on
two embedded GPUs with no cloud. Helix-02 (January 2026) extended control
to the whole body, adding a "System 0" neural locomotion controller trained
on 1,000+ hours of human motion in place of "more than 109,000 lines of
hand-engineered C++"; in May 2026 Figure showed a team running "a full 8-hr
shift". Closed weights.

**Gemini Robotics** (Google DeepMind) *(search; deepmind.google blocked)*:
Gemini Robotics (March 2025) on Gemini 2.0; **On-Device** (24 June 2025),
"the first portable version" that runs on the robot and fine-tunes "with
just 50–100 demos", via an SDK to trusted testers; **1.5** and **ER 1.5**
(25 September 2025) — the VLA that "thinks before taking action", and an
embodied-reasoning model "made broadly available" in the Gemini API and AI
Studio; **Gemini Robotics 2**, **On-Device 2** and **ER 2** (30 July 2026)
— whole-body humanoid control, an on-device model adaptable "with a few
hours of training", ER 2 public in the API, the VLAs to early-access
partners. Closed weights throughout.

## Shapes side by side

| Model | Backbone | Action head | Chunk | Params | Weights |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RT-2 (2023) | PaLI-X 55B / PaLM-E 12B | actions as text tokens | 1 | 12–55B | closed |
| OpenVLA (2024) | Llama-2 7B + DINOv2/SigLIP | discrete tokens (OFT: continuous chunk) | 1 (OFT: 8) | 7B | Llama licence |
| π0 / π0.5 (2024–25) | PaliGemma 3B (Gemma 2B) | flow-matching expert, Gemma 300M | 50 | ~3.3B | Apache-2.0 |
| SmolVLA (2025) | SmolVLM2-500M, 16 layers | flow-matching expert ~100M | 50 | 450M | Apache-2.0 |
| GR00T N1.7 (2026) | Cosmos-Reason2-2B | flow-matching DiT | 40 | 3B | Open Model License |
| X-VLA (2025) | Florence-2 family | flow matching + soft prompts | 32 | 0.9B | Apache-2.0 |
| EO-1 (2025) | Qwen2.5-VL-3B | flow matching | 16 | ~3B | open (licence not read) |
| EVO-1 (2025) | InternVL3-1B | flow matching | 50 | 0.77B | open (licence not read) |
| MolmoAct2 (2026) | Molmo2-ER | flow-matching expert, plus visual trace | — | — | Apache-2.0 |
| WALL-OSS (2025) | Qwen2.5-VL MoE | flow matching or FAST tokens | 32 | — | Apache-2.0 |
| Helix / Helix-02 | ~7B VLM at 7–9 Hz | 80M policy at 200 Hz (+ S0 locomotion) | — | ~7B | closed |
| Gemini Robotics 1.5 / 2 | Gemini | — | — | — | closed; ER in API |

Chunk sizes and backbones are LeRobot's configuration defaults where the
model is in LeRobot; parameter counts are the projects' own figures or
*(search)*.
